clue.text: Copper backing for chimney's unserviceable — cloudy mass results

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: something backing up moves in the opposite direction, so the word for the flue is read from its end

parts.note: lum is a Scottish and northern word for a chimney
US is a short form of unserviceable, as in military jargon

explanation.surface: A broken chimney with copper flashing sends up a cloud of black smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumulus is the meteorological name for heaped, puffy white clouds with rounded tops.

clue.text: Fish left around here in France: more for Will?

indicators.note: going around something means wrapping the outer letters about it

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish
L is the standard abbreviation for left
ici is the French word for here

explanation.surface: A fish left on a French plate prompts a wry question about extra helpings.
explanation.walkthrough: Will looks like a name or willpower; the capital hides a legal will, and the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A codicil is a supplement added to an existing testament, giving extra provisions to a will already made.

clue.text: Mixed muesli about right for disorder

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters wrap around the single letter
mixed ingredients are stirred into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A messy breakfast of muesli makes for chaos in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Misrule means bad government or lawless anarchy, a state of chaos and confusion.

clue.text: Some useful outhouses on the Irish Sea

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a place-name noun

indicators.note: some means only a portion, so the letters are taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join between the two words

explanation.surface: Handy sheds stand somewhere along the coast of the Irish Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Louth is a small county on the east coast of Ireland, facing the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: County Louth lies on Ireland's eastern seaboard, so its coastline borders that stretch of water.

clue.text: Vessel with reduced depth in petrol not to be reported?

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a type of vessel

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter sits within the word for fuel

parts.note: juice is slang for petrol or fuel
depth reduced to its abbreviation D

explanation.surface: A boat runs aground in shallow water, its fuel affair hushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: Sub judice is Latin for 'under a judge': a matter before the courts which the press must not comment on.
explanation.definitionFit: Cases still before a court are legally restricted, so newspapers may not discuss them while proceedings continue.

clue.text: Support the record reserves

parts.note: to back is to support
a log is a written record, as a ship's log

explanation.surface: Someone backs up the official record held in the archive.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is an accumulated store of work or stock held in reserve and not yet used.

clue.text: Beat time in HQ

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one letter goes within the word for headquarters

parts.note: a base is a headquarters
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone keeps the rhythm at headquarters, perhaps a drummer at the barracks.
explanation.definitionFit: To baste can mean to thrash or give someone a beating, an old sense still in dictionaries.

clue.text: What's gone wriggling into fish basket?

definitions.text: What's gone wriggling into fish basket?

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so the jumbled letters go within the basket word

parts.note: a creel is an angler's wicker basket for the catch

indicators.note: something wriggling twists about, so these letters squirm into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An angler asks what has slithered into the wicker basket.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: a long, wriggling sea fish ends up in the creel.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger is a large sea eel, exactly the slippery catch that would squirm its way into a creel.

clue.text: One in deep yen for stage

parts.note: to have a yen is to long for something
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: Someone deep in debt has a yearning for the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a fielder placed far out is 'in the deep'; long leg is one such position, behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Long leg is a cricket fielding position near the boundary, so its fielder stands in the outfield.

clue.text: One could be stuck up one

definitions.text: One could be stuck up one

parts.words: One could be stuck up one
parts.note: surface reading: a person might be stranded somewhere, or something glued up; setter's reading: the idiom for being in difficulty names a sticky, sap-producing tree you can be stranded in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Up a gum tree' is a British idiom for being in trouble with no way out; the second 'one' is the tree itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A eucalyptus exudes resin, and the idiom about being trapped in such a tree means stranded in difficulty.

clue.text: Worry as part of Tweed is turbulent

indicators.note: as part of means only a portion is taken, from inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A worry that the River Tweed is running rough and dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tweed is a river on the border between England and Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb someone is to trouble or unsettle them, the same as making them anxious.

clue.text: One's the same as another

parts.note: surface reading: two people or things are identical; setter's reading: a word that means the same as a different word

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a remark about lookalikes; the thing that is 'the same as another' is a word of equal meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Words with matching meanings are interchangeable in a sentence, which is precisely what this term describes.

clue.text: Golf property round bush, somehow, in tip?

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters are placed inside the word for a tip

parts.note: a tip is a hint, which is a clue

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are arranged in some new way

parts.note: round gives O, the ring-shaped letter, and bush is taken as written

explanation.surface: A golf club's building near some shrubbery, given as a hot tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a rubbish dump but is a hint. O ('round') and BUSH are shuffled together and then placed 'in' the hint word.
explanation.definitionFit: The members' building at a golf course is a piece of property owned by the club.

clue.text: The French in their way backing Swiss mathematician

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the French article sits within the other piece
backing means moving in reverse, so the word for a street is read from its end

parts.note: rue is the French word for a street or way, 'their' pointing back to the French
le is a French word for the

explanation.surface: The French are reversing to support a renowned Swiss mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: Leonhard Euler was an 18th-century Swiss mathematician.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was a celebrated Swiss scholar of numbers, analysis and geometry born in Basel.

clue.text: The city's to the fore, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its spoken sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to be to the fore is to be ahead of others

explanation.surface: A boast that a city is in front of its rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a major English urban centre in West Yorkshire, and so a city.

clue.text: Bird with grit, a music-maker

parts.note: sand is fine grit
a piper plays the pipes

explanation.surface: A bird with plenty of pluck is also a fine musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grit' looks like courage, but here it is the loose material of a beach.
explanation.definitionFit: The sandpiper is a small wading shorebird with a long bill, found on beaches and mudflats.

clue.text: Plant class in US universities

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
a league is a class or grade, as in 'not in the same league'

explanation.surface: A botany class is being taught at American colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: The name comes from the ivy grown on the old buildings of these colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is the group of eight old, prestigious north-eastern American colleges such as Harvard and Yale.

clue.text: 1Standard credit when supporting quads

parts.note: quads are quadrangles, enclosed courtyards or yards
tick is informal British for credit, as in buying 'on tick'

explanation.surface: A standard rule applies when credit is backing a set of quad bikes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' means placed below, so the courtyards come first. The stray '1' before 'Standard' is a typo in the source.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measure used as a benchmark against which other things are judged.

clue.text: English actor run possibly as a storyteller

indicators.note: possibly means one of several ways it might go, so the letters could be in another order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An English performer might go on to become a teller of tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone who tells anecdotes skilfully and entertainingly, a gifted spinner of tales.

clue.text: Tries PE after injury suspension

indicators.note: something after an injury is damaged and out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A pupil tries gym class again after being hurt and is then sidelined.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is physical education, the school sports lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a pause or temporary halt, just as a suspension is an interval of stopping.

clue.text: Wires could be passed transversely

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tangled, as in a misunderstanding of ... wires
second meaning: went across from one side to the other

explanation.surface: Electrical cables may be routed across one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossed wires' is an idiom for a misunderstanding; the first definition completes that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes lines that intersect, and also the past tense of going over from side to side.

clue.text: Spot produced by insect mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the locust is a swarming grasshopper

explanation.surface: A mark on the skin was caused by a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Locus is Latin for place, used in English for a particular position or point.

clue.text: Firm place in church for thick black liquid

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
the altar is the table at the front of a church

explanation.surface: A business sets aside a spot in a church for a dark, sticky substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal tar is the dark viscous by-product of making coke or gas from coal.

clue.text: Deed, say, upsetting, as sorrowful one could be

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An unkind act is distressing, and its victim is left looking miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: A grieving person looks mournful, with melancholy in their gaze, so they appear that way.

clue.text: Ship's funds going west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means running right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: pools are shared funds, money gathered together

explanation.surface: A ship's money is lost, as in 'gone west'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going west' sounds like the idiom for being lost; here it means reading right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing vessel, so it is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Blow the directors! I have the controls

parts.note: dash is a mild oath, as in 'dash it!', like 'blow!'
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: An exasperated executive curses the board who keep overruling them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' and 'dash' are both mild old-fashioned exclamations of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dashboard is the panel in a car carrying the instruments and switches, so it holds the controls.

clue.text: The tot's pop?

parts.note: surface reading: a small child's fizzy drink; setter's reading: pop is a familiar word for father, so the child's name for a dad

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' suggests a soft drink; it is an informal word for a father, and a small child's word for him is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Young children call their father by this affectionate pet name, the nursery word for a dad.

clue.text: Note uprising ropes in crude strength

indicators.note: to rope something in is to draw it inside, so the outer letters enclose another word
in a down clue, rising up means reading from bottom to top, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: NB, nota bene, means note well
raw means crude or unrefined

explanation.surface: A note about a rebellion that gains support through brute force.
explanation.definitionFit: Brawn means muscular physical power, as opposed to brains.

clue.text: Colourless flat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lacking character or interest

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of a painted flat; both words separately describe something dull.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes food without flavour and people or writing without vigour, matching both dull senses.

clue.text: Play with tin scraps in an unsuitable way

indicators.note: scraps are broken bits, so the letters are smashed and reassembled in another order

parts.note: taken as written, skipping the joining word, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A child amuses themself with tin offcuts, which is hardly appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two words of fodder and adds no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, so the adverb describes doing something in an ill-fitting manner.

clue.text: Old tree: 50 years?

parts.note: the elder is a small tree with white flowers and dark berries
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Y is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: An ancient tree that has stood for fifty years.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly describes people of advanced age, getting on in years.

clue.text: Diner, perhaps, placed between king and duke's relatives

parts.note: K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

indicators.note: perhaps means maybe, so the word might appear in some other arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A guest at dinner sits between a king and a duke, all related.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred means one's family and blood relations, used as a collective noun for kin.
